Hyprland 0.56.2 IPC traffic captured from a live session in one run of
scripts/capture-hyprland.sh 300: the owner's laptop, Hyprland 0.56.2
(efb5099, version.json) with three monitors (eDP-1 1920x1200, DP-6 and
DP-2 1920x1080), 2026-10-12, read-only (no dispatch, keyword or reload
was sent by the script; the owner ran `hyprctl reload` in a terminal).

start/  the replies to j/monitors, j/workspaces, j/clients and
        j/activewindow, read while the stream was quiet, before its first
        line (marks.txt "start 0"). Three windows on workspaces 1, 2 (DP-2)
        and 6 (DP-6), workspace 12 empty on eDP-1, DP-6 focused.
events.txt  every line of .socket2.sock for about 300 s (287 lines).
end/    the same four replies read after its last line ("end 287"). The
        structure is the start's; the focus is on DP-2.

What the owner did, in order (the stream shows each): DP-2 unplugged and
plugged back (Hyprland moves its workspaces 1 and 2 to eDP-1 before
monitorremoved, and back before monitoradded; the layer shells close and
reopen), windows opened and closed, a window moved to new workspaces 4
and 5 and back, fullscreen on and off twice, the special workspace
special:magic shown and hidden with a terminal on it, `hyprctl reload`
run from that terminal (configreloaded), the special workspace made and
destroyed again, and focus moved between the monitors while a terminal's
title spun (◐ ◑ ✳).

Scrubbed, the same way in replies and events: two terminal session titles
by "term one" and "term two" (their spinner glyphs kept), the shell
prompt's user and host by "user@host", and the two DP monitors' serial
numbers by SERIAL00001 and SERIAL00002 (in their description). Not
scrubbed, as captured: window classes (public app ids), the capture
command's own title, layer namespaces, addresses, stableIds, pids, and
the monitors' make and model.

src/wm/hyprland.rs's tests captured_session_events_are_each_handled and
captured_session_ends_where_hyprland_does replay it; the adapter needed no
change for it. With hyprland-0.56.2-captured it covers what that capture
did not: a second (and third) monitor, hotplug, closewindow, movewindow,
fullscreen, configreloaded and special workspaces.
